data.gender_notes: Jaganath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jaganath is derived from the Sanskrit words Jagat (universe) and Ish (Lord), meaning 'Lord of the Universe'. In Hinduism, Jaganath is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to protect and nurture the universe and all its beings. The name Jaganath carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Jaganath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Jaganath is a powerful and revered name in Hinduism, representing the divine protector and nurturer of the universe. It is a name that evokes a sense of strength, peace, and spiritual connection.
data.etymology: Jaganath belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaganath total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jaganath has held significant importance in Hindu culture for centuries. It is one of the popular names of Lord Vishnu, and shrines dedicated to Lord Jaganath are found all across the Indian subcontinent. The name has been included in various Hindu scriptures, including the Bhagavata Purana, which describes Lord Jaganath as a form of Mahavisnu who assumes ordinariness to hide his divine form from common people and protect them from the wrath of Lord Shiva and other demons. Additionally, Lord Jaganath's shrine at Puri in Odisha, India, is a major pilgrimage site for Hindus and draws millions of devotees every year.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Jaganath lies in its representation of the divine protector and sustainer of the universe. Lord Jaganath is believed to be the embodiment of compassion, love, and kindness towards all beings, and is often invoked for protection, guidance, and blessings. The name is a reminder that despite the vastness and complexity of the universe, there is a divine power that watches over and cares for all living beings. Devotion to Lord Jaganath is believed to bring peace, happiness, and spiritual growth to one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jaganath, meaning "Lord of the Universe," represents the all-pervading form of Vishnu, symbolizing the infinite cosmic power and compassion that nurtures and protects all beings.

historical_references.reference: Jaganath is a form of Lord Vishnu, also known as Jagannatha, Jagannath, or Jagannatha Deva. He is the presiding deity of the temple at Puri in Odisha, India.
historical_references.context: Jaganath is a popular deity in Hinduism and is considered to be the supreme God and the ruler of the universe.

trends: Jaganath is a popular name among Hindus, especially in Odisha, India.
